"''Oh, I've won a lot of things. I once won a subtropical moon in the Oseon Belt.|Han Solo and Lando Calrissian|}} The '''Oseon Belt''' was a part of the [[Oseon system]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]]' [[Centrality]]. It contained a [[Unidentified subtropical moon|subtropical moon]] which the [[gambler]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] won ownership of at one point by [[10 BBY]]. By [[3 ABY|thirteen years]] later, the gambler [[Zana Gatta]] was expelled from the Oseon [[Star system|system]] after apparently breaking the rules of the [[gaamja]] game during a match in the Oseon Belt. ==Description== [[File:Oseon-TFABG.jpg|thumb|right|300px|The Oseon Belt was located in the Oseon system.]] The Oseon Belt was situated in the [[Oseon system]] of the [[Centrality]] region. It was a part of the regions known as the [[Outer Rim Territories]] and [[the Slice]]. Along with the rest of the Oseon [[Star system|system]], the Oseon Belt was located in grid square T-8 of the [[Standard Galactic Grid]] and lay on a [[hyperspace route]] that linked it to the [[Junkfort Station system|Junkfort Station]] and [[Marleyvane system]]s.{{TheStarWarsGalaxy}} Another route, known as the [[Sanity Skip]], also connected the Oseon system to the [[Kessel system]]. The Oseon Belt contained a [[Unidentified subtropical moon|subtropical moon]]. ==History== {{Quote|Friend of mine saw her at a gaamja match in the Oseon Belt last cycle. Apparently she tried to palm the disc. They kicked her out of the whole system for that one.|A Rodian, on Zana Gatta|''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]''}} At some point by [[10 BBY]],''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' dates the portions of ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' set on [[Vandor]] and on [[Numidian Prime]] to [[10 BBY]]. the [[human]] [[gambler]] [[Landonis Balthazar Calrissian|Lando Calrissian]] won ownership of the Oseon Belt's subtropical [[moon]]. in a game of cards. That [[Standard year|year]], Calrissian mentioned his acquisition of the natural satellite during a game of [[sabacc]] with the [[thief]] [[Han Solo]] in the [[Cantina|saloon]] known as [[the Lodge]] on the [[planet]] [[Vandor]].''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' In [[3 ABY]],{{OutlawsDate}} [[flight FY-47]] to the Oseon Belt that was scheduled to depart from [[Mirogana Spaceport]]'s [[gate W1]] on the moon [[Toshara]] of the Outer Rim's [[Shadola sector]] was cancelled after the moon's [[Galactic Empire]] [[Governor]] [[Thorden]] closed down a section of the [[spaceport]]. A [[cycle]] earlier, the human gambler [[Zana Gatta]] participated in a match of [[gaamja]] in the Oseon Belt that was witnessed by a friend of a [[Unidentified Rodian gambler (Morenia)|Rodian]]. For an apparent breaking of the game's rules, Gatta was expelled from the Oseon system.''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]'' {{Gamemechanics|Star Wars Outlaws|canon=1}} In 3 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|ABY]],{{OutlawsDate}} the [[Rodian]] shared details about Gatta's match in the Oseon Belt with the [[thief]] [[Kay Vess]] while they were both aboard the [[casino cruiser]] ''[[Morenia]]''. {{Endgame}} ==Behind the scenes== [[File:Solo_A_Star_Wars_Story_Theatrical_Poster.png|thumb|right|250px|''Solo: A Star Wars Story'' saw the first mention of the Oseon Belt.]] The Oseon Belt was first mentioned in the [[2018]] ''[[Star Wars Anthology Series]]'' film ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''. The accompanying reference book ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' by [[Pablo Hidalgo]] spelled its name as the "Oseon belt." The origins of the Oseon Belt lie in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity. ''[[Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu]]'',''[[Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu]]'' the [[June 12]], [[1983]]''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, New Edition]]'' first entry in [[Star Wars: The Lando Calrissian Adventures|''The Lando Calrissian Adventures'']] trilogy of novels by [[L. Neil Smith]], saw the first appearance of the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]]-filled [[Oseon system/Legends|Oseon system]]. That [[Star system/Legends|star system]] was then established to have contained multiple [[Asteroid field/Legends|asteroid belts]] by the trilogy's''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]'' [[September 12]], 1983 second entry, ''[[Lando Calrissian and the Flamewind of Oseon]]''. On that book's original cover, an illustration by [[William Schmidt]] also provided the first visual depiction of the system's asteroid [[Oseon 6845]]. "[[Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are]]," a [[1990]] [[Roleplaying game|roleplaying]] source article published in the [[Voyages SF 13|thirteenth issue]] of the ''[[Voyages SF]]'' magazine, referred to the Oseon system's group of asteroids as a more [[Oseon asteroid belt|unitary object]], referring to it as the "Oseon Belt" and describing it as a singular asteroid belt. Since that article was released outside of the [[Lucas Licensing]] process, its [[canon]]icity with respect to ''Star Wars'' Legends was never confirmed.{{VoyagesCite|13|Twinkle, Twinkle Little Star, How I Wonder Where We Are}} [[File:Oseon6845-LCA.png|thumb|left|250px|''Star Wars'' Legends depiction of the Oseon Asteroid Belt's asteroid Oseon 6845]] Beginning with the [[1996]] ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]'' rulebook authored by [[Bill Smith]] for use with [[West End Games]]' ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game, Second Edition, Revised and Expanded]]'' as well as Hidalgo's 1996 [[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|Second Edition]] of[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back (Second Edition)|''Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back'', Second Edition]] the [[1989]] ''The Roleplaying Game'' sourcebook ''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'',''[[Galaxy Guide 3: The Empire Strikes Back]]'' unambiguously canonical ''[[Star Wars]]'' sources began following suit,''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''{{CSWECite|II|313-314|''Millennium Falcon''}}{{CSWECite|II|426|Oseon}}{{CSWECite|II|427|Oseon, Gadfrey}}''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' introducing nomenclature such as the "Oseon asteroid belt," the "Oseon asteroid field," and the "Oseon belt." The [[Wizards of the Coast]] [[Star Wars Roleplaying Game|roleplaying game]] source article "[[A Campaign Guide to the Centrality]]," which was authored by [[Michael Kogge]] and published in the [[Star Wars Gamer 5|fifth issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars Gamer]]'' magazine{{GamerCite|5|A Campaign Guide to the Centrality}} on [[July 24]], [[2001]],{{SWArchive|url=gaming/other/rpg/news20010627.html|text=''Gamer'' #5. A Domain of Evil it is.}} was the first work to attempt to reconcile the two perspectives by characterizing the overall object, which it referred to as the "Oseon Asteroid Belt," as indeed consisting of several smaller belts. ==Appearances== *''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' {{1stm}} *''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition]]'' {{Ab|Solo: A Star Wars Story: Expanded Edition (audiobook)}} {{Mo}} *''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story: A Junior Novel]]'' {{Ab|Solo: A Star Wars Story: A Junior Novel (audiobook)}} {{Mo}} *[[Solo: A Star Wars Story Adaptation 3|''Solo: A Star Wars Story Adaptation'' 3]] {{Mo}} *''[[Star Wars Outlaws]]'' {{Mo}} {{DLC|''Wild Card''}} ==Sources== *''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]'' ==Notes and references== {{Reflist}} {{Interlang |es=Cinturón de Oseon |fr=Ceinture d'Oseon }} [[Category:Astronomical objects in the Outer Rim Territories]] [[Category:Astronomical objects in the Slice]] [[Category:Oseon system locations]]
